description: The multidimensional unreplicated linear functional relationship (MULFR) model compares two sets of p-dimensional variables—graduate competencies and industry expectations—both measured with error via questionnaires, yielding a single coefficient of determination.
title: MULFR model with R² as a competency gap measure for multidimensional self-report data

description: This capture pattern combines eye-level, bird's-eye-view, and close-up turntable videos so that material movements are analytically visible.
title: Multi-angle video capture for human–material analysis

description: The report's guidance is that analysts running studies with several intervention arms should not simply reuse two-group methods: estimators \"need to be modified for the multi-armed design,\" hypothesis tests across pairwise contrasts require multiple comparison adjustments, and CACE estimation demand
title: Multi-armed randomized trial analysis

description: The article offers a detailed methodology for studying how engagement and achievement evolve together across a full program: two chronologically ordered state sequences (engagement and achievement channels) are aligned per course, and a Mixture Hidden Markov Model — \"a combination of LCA and HMM\" —
title: Multi-channel sequence analysis with mixture hidden Markov models

description: The MCA is the article's own methodological framework for combining quantitative and qualitative evidence under a single roof, grounded in constructivist learning theory and the Gestalt holistic approach.
title: Multi-complementary approach (MCA): three-stage mixed-methods evaluation framework

description: The article proposes a multi-dimensional approach to analyzing argumentative knowledge construction in CSCL.
title: Multi-dimensional analysis approach for CSCL discourse corpora

description: A multi-dimensional coding procedure for analyzing small group chat communication in CSCL research, developed by the authors to address three methodological issues: \"the unit of analysis and unit fragmentation\", \"the reconstruction of the response structure\" and \"determining reliability without over
title: Multi-dimensional coding procedure for small group chat communication

description: The article names competency bias as \"the inherent tendency of preference-tuned models to produce correct solutions even when prompted to simulate novice students\", and frames simulating learners as a multi-dimensional fidelity problem with behavioral, epistemic, and perceptual components.
title: Multi-dimensional fidelity framework for LLM student simulation

description: A computational framework combining three analytical channels applied to workplace-based assessment data: \"(i) a set of features for analysing clinical skills WBA data, (ii) analysis of the temporal aspects of that data using process mining, and (iii) utilising text analytics to compare student refl
title: Multi-faceted data-driven assessment analytics approach for workplace learning

description: The article builds a multi-label classifier by revising \"the standard BERT model from a class-independent model to five binary BERT classifiers for each category\", one per cognitive presence category.
title: Multi-label BERT classification of cognitive presence in MOOC discussion messages

description: The framework holds that analysis of digital learner interactions should differentiate three overlapping processes: posting activity at the individual level, communication structures as learner-to-learner projections, and emergent relational structures as filtered backbones of communication networks
title: Multi-level framework separating posting activity, communication structures, and emergent relational structures in online discussions

description: The article develops a framework in which three methods answer complementary questions about networked learning: social network analysis to find out \"who is talking to whom\", content analysis of coded learning and tutoring activities to find out \"what they are talking about\", and contextual analysis
title: Multi-method research framework combining SNA, content analysis and contextual analysis for networked learning

description: The article introduces a model for estimating growth from longitudinal data in which multiple raters evaluate a construct such as a student's self-efficacy.
title: Multi-rater latent growth curve model

description: A novel evaluation protocol in which a fine-tuned student model and a candidate tutor model generate synthetic multi-turn dialogues that are scored by conversational statistics and a reasoning LLM judge, with results aggregated.
title: Multi-turn synthetic-dialogue evaluation protocol for AI tutors

description: Siette addresses the mismatch between the fine-grained multidimensional learner models of ITSs and the single-latent-trait focus of CTT and IRT through a multi-unidimensional approach.
title: Multi-unidimensional approach to bridging psychometric and ITS learner models

description: The article presents multiagent, time- and space-synchronized first-person perspective analysis (FPA) as a method for capturing observer-independent behavioral metrics during emergency simulation training.
title: Multiagent first-person perspective analysis (FPA)

description: The article proposes an evaluation framework for educational question-answering models that combines automatic text metrics with structured-output features and bootstrap confidence intervals.
title: Multidimensional evaluation framework separating reference-answer similarity, structured-output stability, and domain-specific correctness

description: The review proposes an organizing framework for systematically analysing studies that compare VR-based and traditional teaching in higher education.
title: Multidimensional framework for analysing comparative VR-vs-traditional studies in higher education

description: Multidimensional Recurrence Quantification Analysis (MdRQA) is the analytic method the article uses to quantify physiological synchrony in multivariate EDA time series.
title: Multidimensional Recurrence Quantification Analysis (MdRQA) with surrogate-data comparison

description: The review establishes a multidisciplinary taxonomy that organizes the broad range of educational interventions to counter community violence into distinguishable approaches.
title: Multidisciplinary taxonomy of educational approaches to counter community violence

description: This analytical pattern combines several learning-analytics methods into layers to capture role dynamics over time: latent class analysis converts CoI-coded discourse into role states, epistemic network analysis maps code co-occurrence within roles, sequence mining orders roles across weeks, and Mar
title: Multilayered temporal analysis of collaborative-learning roles

description: MAIHDA (Multilevel Analysis of Individual Heterogeneity and Discriminatory Accuracy) is a statistical framework in which individuals are nested within intersectional strata defined by combinations of social categories.
title: Multilevel Analysis of Individual Heterogeneity and Discriminatory Accuracy (MAIHDA)

description: The article conceptualizes teachers' autonomy support as a multilevel construct with distinct operationalizations: class-directed support measured with class-referent items forms an L2 climate construct reflecting the \"overall classroom-specific autonomy-supportive climate\"; individual support is an
title: Multilevel conceptualization of autonomy support: climate, contextual, and perceived-difference constructs

description: The article proposes a multilevel framework for understanding variability in GenAI-mediated writing outcomes.
title: Multilevel conceptualization of moderators in GenAI-mediated writing research (technological, learner, and contextual factors)

description: The article recaps Lüdtke et al.'s (2008) multilevel latent covariate model, in which students' ratings of classroom climate are latently aggregated to a latent class mean that is regressed on an outcome at the class level.
title: Multilevel latent covariate model for unbiased estimation of class-level climate–outcome relations

description: The multilevel LTA–MixIRTM extends latent transition analysis by incorporating a mixture IRT measurement model into a two-level LTA, so that \"change can be accounted for as a transition from one latent class to another and as progress or lack thereof along a latent continuous variable (e.g., ability
title: Multilevel latent transition analysis with a mixture IRT measurement model (multilevel LTA–MixIRTM)

description: The article introduces the ML-LVM, in which each rater's judgments are modeled with a rater-specific bivariate normal distribution whose mean, variance, and covariance parameters correspond to the level, differentiation, and rank components of judgment accuracy.
title: Multilevel latent variable model (ML-LVM) of judgment accuracy

description: This methodological framework treats VLE usage as a discrete latent variable: latent class analyses at student and classroom levels characterize usage patterns, generalized propensity scores with inverse probability weighting remove selection bias into classes, and Vermunt's three-step method accoun
title: Multilevel mixture modeling with propensity score weights operationalizing VLE usage as latent classes

description: The article argues that research on teacher motivation and instruction should not neglect the school context: teachers' self-efficacy should be modeled both as an individual variable and as a school-level composite, and school characteristics (collective efficacy, collaboration, participation, leade
title: Multilevel modeling of teacher self-efficacy and instructional quality across teacher and school levels

description: The article presents multilevel modelling as a statistical approach for hierarchically clustered data in collaborative learning research, in which messages are nested within students (and measurement occasions) within groups.
title: Multilevel modelling of hierarchically clustered CSCL content-analysis data

description: The pipeline vectorizes English and German think-aloud utterances with OpenAI's text-embedding-3-small, \"a pre- trained sentence embedding model that converts textual input into a high-dimensional vector with a length of 1,536\".
title: Multilingual embedding-based automated classification of self-regulated-learning think-aloud utterances

description: Multimodal analysis is one of three methodological advances the report highlights, defined as \"Integrating multiple streams of data, such as audio, video, eye gaze, sensors, and clickstream data.\" The introduction elaborates it as \"the study of learning with data streams that include physical moveme
title: Multimodal analysis

description: A computational framework that jointly predicts a continuous engagement score in [1,5] and a binary label from tutoring-video clips.
title: Multimodal engagement-prediction framework with Perceiver IO fusion, hierarchical Bayesian participant context, and uncertainty-aware heads

description: The article adopts a methodological framework combining eye-tracking with think-aloud protocols to capture students' real-time engagement with rubrics during academic tasks.
title: Multimodal process-tracing approach to rubric use

description: Because the basic single-group ITS depends on extrapolating the pretest functional form as a counterfactual, an assumption the authors call problematic, evaluators should add multiple design elements to the basic ITS structure.
title: Multiple-design-element interrupted time series evaluation

description: The paper develops a 'multipurpose' study design that fuses survey sampling and experimental design results so that a single study can answer three generalization questions: the average effect, its variability, and treatment effect moderation.
title: Multipurpose design framework for answering three generalization questions in behavioral science experiments

description: This study adopts a multivariate extension of Bayesian Causal Forests (BCF), a non-parametric causal inference machine learning model built on Bayesian Additive Regression Trees.
title: Multivariate Bayesian Causal Forests

description: The report uses a model-based approach in which observed scores are decomposed into true scores and error scores, with the standard error of measurement introduced so that imprecision of observed scores is accounted for.
title: Multivariate true score model for achievement and growth norming

description: The review advocates a network approach in which motivation and achievement constructs are nodes and bidirectional partial correlations are edges, so constructs emerge empirically as clusters rather than being assumed a priori.
title: Mutualistic network approach to motivation-achievement relations
